bio.short: Yuxuan Chen is an M.S. student at Tianjin University who builds physics-guided machine-learning models for viscoelastic and complex flows.
bio.standard: Yuxuan Chen is a third-year M.S. student in Power Engineering and Engineering Thermophysics at Tianjin University, advised by Prof. Hongna Zhang. The work starts from a practical gap in viscoelastic turbulence: experiments can measure velocity, but not the polymer stress that drives the flow. PhySF-UNO, published in Physics of Fluids, reconstructs the full conformation tensor from velocity with a Fourier-operator U-Net and a positive-definiteness constraint. FAMIR, the follow-up project, uses the future state available during training to make long recursive flow forecasts drift less, tested on viscoelastic channel flow, Rayleigh–Bénard convection and rotating shallow water. Before this, Yuxuan studied engineering mechanics at Tianjin University and spent a summer at the AI for Science Institute, Beijing, building generative models for centrifugal sprays. Yuxuan is applying for PhD programs starting in Fall 2027.
bio.extended: Yuxuan Chen is a third-year M.S. student in Power Engineering and Engineering Thermophysics at Tianjin University, advised by Prof. Hongna Zhang, after a B.Eng. in Engineering Mechanics at the same university. The undergraduate thesis used OpenFOAM to simulate drag reduction and heat transfer of viscoelastic fluids in a natural-circulation safety system, and the high-Weissenberg cases that were hard to compute led directly to machine learning. PhySF-UNO, published in Physics of Fluids, reconstructs the hidden polymer conformation tensor from velocity fields in elasto-inertial turbulence; Fourier blocks on the U-Net skip connections capture the non-local coupling, and a positive-definiteness loss cuts non-physical tensors from about 24% to 0.05%. FAMIR asks how to forecast such flows stably: a teacher that sees the true next state and a student that sees only the history drive one shared latent transition, and only the student is deployed. At the AI for Science Institute, Beijing, Yuxuan built a CGAN–CVAE framework that predicts centrifugal-spray images and cone angles from nozzle conditions, which received an Outstanding Paper Award at the CSET annual conference. Yuxuan is applying for PhD programs starting in Fall 2027.

about.lead: Machine learning that respects the physics of viscoelastic and complex flows: reconstructing the stress we cannot measure, and forecasting flows that stay stable over long horizons.
about.where_body: Next steps: reconstructing polymer stress from sparse, noisy PIV data; generative and stochastic reconstruction with uncertainty; and stable learned surrogates and closures that can sit inside real simulations.

about: I am a third-year M.S. student in Power Engineering and Engineering Thermophysics at Tianjin University, advised by Prof. Hongna Zhang. I received my B.Eng. in Engineering Mechanics from Tianjin University in 2024. In the summer of 2025 I was a research intern in the DeepFlame team at the AI for Science Institute, Beijing (AISI), working with Prof. Zhi X. Chen.

I use physics-guided machine learning to study viscoelastic and complex flows. Experiments can measure velocity but not the polymer stress that drives elastic turbulence, so my first project reconstructs the conformation tensor from velocity with a neural operator that keeps the tensor positive definite. My second project, FAMIR, asks how to forecast such flows stably over long horizons.
I am applying for PhD programs starting in Fall 2027.
interests: Physics-guided machine learning for viscoelastic and elasto-inertial turbulence
